title: Signals backend: error logs, feedback and bugs tables
description: Add supabase/migrations with error_logs (clustered by hash, upsert_error_log function), app_feedback and bugs tables, RLS, and a db:push-staging script, so the signal adapter in .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/signal-adapter.md has data to read. Forks get this by default. Admin = a role claim in the user's auth app_metadata (never user_metadata, which users can edit); admins and local dev can read, signed-in users can insert their own rows. Test it on a scratch Postgres, then apply it to the project; with isolated staging, staging first and production after merge.

title: Configure Supabase
description: Set up the backend: one Supabase project with the auth providers you use enabled, its Site URL set to the app's primary origin, and its URL and publishable key available as VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (local .env, plus the hosting build variables for main and for previews). Before the app has real users, isolate staging from production with a Supabase Branching staging branch or a second project (documentation/DOC_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS.md § Staging backend). Your coding agent lists the exact requirements, checks the result, and tells you what only you can do. For Google sign-in, requirements are in documentation/DOC_SUPABASE_GOOGLE_OAUTH.md. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Configuration tasks gate (Supabase).

title: Put your app online (Cloudflare hosting)
description: Get your app live on the internet with Cloudflare (free tier is fine). Your coding agent does the setup — just ask it to "do the hosting task". What you need ready: a Cloudflare account, your Supabase keys already in .env, and (optional) a domain name you own. How it works once set up depends on your git workflow mode (see .claude/rules/git-workflow.md § Mode behavior table, rows staging and production) — by default every pull request gets its own preview link and merging the pull request ships to production. One step happens in the Cloudflare website (connecting your repo); the agent tells you what must be set there and why, waits for you, and checks the result. Agent playbook + troubleshooting: documentation/DOC_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS.md (see "Agent one-shot brief"). Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Configuration tasks gate (Hosting).

title: Define app vision
description: Collaborate with the coding agent to fill documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md (problem, persona, app role). Replace placeholder bullets with real prose and change Vision status from DRAFT to ACTIVE when complete. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § App vision & goals gate.

title: Configure Theme
description: Restyle the app via design tokens in src/index.css (light values in :root, dark in .dark): brand colors, radius, density, fonts. See documentation/DOC_THEMING.md. Verify both modes with the theme icon in the profile menu. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Configuration tasks gate (Theme).

title: Capture app errors to the database
description: Global window error and unhandledrejection handler, error boundary reporting, and the existing logError path, all writing through the deduplicating upsert from the signals backend task. Tag each error with the environment (local, staging, production). Depends on: Signals backend task.

title: In-app feedback widget
description: A small signed-in feedback form that writes to app_feedback with the page and environment. Depends on: Signals backend task.

title: Admin signals view and switch the signal adapter on
description: An admin-only view (role claim) to triage error clusters and feedback, and turn on loop-backlog's signal adapter so open signals become ranked backlog tasks. Depends on: Signals backend, error capture and feedback widget tasks.

title: Add a db:push-staging script or fix the adapter reference
description: The signal adapter (.agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/signal-adapter.md) tells the agent to run `pnpm run db:push-staging`, which does not exist. Either add a script that applies supabase/migrations to the staging project with a pinned Supabase CLI (needs project linking, which the owner must set up), or change the adapter to say the connector or CLI applies migrations. Protected file edit: needs owner approval. Context: documentation/DOC_DECISION_LOG.md § signals-backend D8.
